To evaluate whether overdispersion and excess zeros distort inference
in the needle-sharing dataset,
we fit a [negative binomial regression model](#def-nb-reg)
with the same [covariates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-covariate)
as the baseline [Poisson regression model](#def-poisson-reg),
and compare its coefficient [estimates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-estimate)
and [standard errors](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-SE)
against that [Poisson model](#def-poisson-reg).

```{r}
#| label: fit-nb-model
# fit the negative binomial model by direct maximum likelihood,
# with the same covariates as the Poisson model `glm1`
glm1_nb <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(
  formula = shared_syr ~ homeless +
    age + sex + ethn + polydrug + hivstat + sexabuse + hplsns,
  family = glmmTMB::nbinom2,
  data = needles
)
```

::: notes
We fit this model with `glmmTMB::glmmTMB()` [@brooks2017glmmTMB],
which maximizes the [likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-lik)
over the [coefficients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-linear-combination)
of the [linear predictor](Intro-to-GLMs.qmd#def-linear-predictor)
and $\rho$ jointly.
`MASS::glm.nb()` [@venables2002modern] instead alternates between
[iteratively reweighted least squares](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/logistic-inference.html#def-irls) for the coefficients
and a separate fit of $\rho$.
On these data the [sequence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-sequence) of alternating fits does not
[converge](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-convergent-sequence).
`glm.nb()` warns "alternation limit reached", <!-- check-term-links: allow: "limit" here is part of a quoted R warning, not a mathematical limit -->
and on some platforms it stops with an R error instead. <!-- check-term-links: allow: an R error message, not a statistical error -->
The `nbinom2` family in `glmmTMB` has [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) $\mu + \mu^2 / \rho$,
matching @eq-nb-reg-var,
and `sigma(glm1_nb)` returns $\est{\rho}$.
:::

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Negative binomial model for needle-sharing data"
#| label: tbl-needles-nb
# show the log-mean coefficients, on the same scale as the comparison table
glm1_nb |>
  parameters() |>
  print_md()
```

---

Evaluating the estimated parameters across models reveals
how accounting for overdispersion affects inference.
The coefficient for homelessness, the exposure of interest,
changes little between the [Poisson](#def-poisson-reg) and [negative binomial models](#def-nb-reg),
while several adjustment [coefficients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-linear-combination) shift substantially,
and some change sign.
The [negative binomial](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-nb) standard errors are several times
the Poisson standard errors,
reflecting the excess variability of the [outcome](Intro-to-GLMs.qmd#def-outcome).

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Poisson vs. Negative Binomial regression estimates"
#| label: tbl-compare-poisson-nb
tibble(
  Parameter = names(coef(glm1)),
  `Poisson Coef` = coef(glm1),
  `Poisson SE` = summary(glm1)$coefficients[, "Std. Error"],
  `NB Coef` = glmmTMB::fixef(glm1_nb)$cond,
  `NB SE` = summary(glm1_nb)$coefficients$cond[, "Std. Error"]
) |>
  pander::pander()
```

{{< slidebreak >}}

#### Zero-inflated models for needle-sharing

Because many participants report zero shared syringes in the past 30 days,
we fit a zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) model
to distinguish structural non-sharers from count variability.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Zero-inflated Poisson model"
#| label: tbl-zeroinf-poisson
library(glmmTMB)
zinf_pois <- glmmTMB(
  family = "poisson",
  data = needles,
  formula = shared_syr ~ homeless +
    age + sex + ethn + polydrug + hivstat + sexabuse + hplsns,
  # the zero-inflation submodel uses the exposure, matching Vittinghoff's
  # `inflate(i.homeless)` (@vittinghoff2e, §8.3.1)
  ziformula = ~ homeless
)

zinf_pois |>
  parameters(exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  print_md()
```

::: notes

Another R package for zero-inflated models is
[`pscl`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pscl/index.html) (@pscl08).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

#### Zero-inflated negative binomial model

To combine flexible dispersion modeling with zero-inflation,
we also fit a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Zero-inflated negative binomial model"
#| label: tbl-zeroinf-nb
zinf_nb <- glmmTMB(
  family = nbinom2,
  data = needles,
  formula = shared_syr ~ homeless +
    age + sex + ethn + polydrug + hivstat + sexabuse + hplsns,
  ziformula = ~ homeless
)

zinf_nb |>
  parameters(exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  print_md()
```

::: notes
Both zero-inflated models keep the zero-inflation (structural-zero) submodel
parsimonious --- just the exposure, `ziformula = ~ homeless` ---
matching @vittinghoff2e's `inflate(i.homeless)` [§8.3.1].

A richer zero-inflation submodel is poorly identified here.
With the negative binomial in particular,
the overdispersion parameter and the zero-inflation component
both compete to explain the excess zeros,
so adding several covariates to the submodel makes the logistic fit
*separate*: its coefficients diverge and the exponentiated estimates
([odds ratios](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-OR)) run off to $\pm\infty$.
Keeping the submodel small avoids that.
:::
